label: Early copy phase of long sequences, when the fed-back input is one of 3/1/d/q/x/y/c/2/f
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase: never on original tokens or <DEL>, and never at recall_idx 0. Rate is about 12% of copy steps. It is concentrated in long sequences (L=9 holds 56% of mass, L>=8 holds 83%; almost nothing for L<=5) and peaks at recall_idx 2-3 (the second and third copy outputs, t=10-12), dips in the middle, then rises again at the last outputs of L=9. Token identity of the fed-back input strongly modulates the rate: 3, 1 and d (about 20%) are highest, then q, x, y, c, 2, f; the output token matters too (x, 3, c, t). Rate also goes up with the number of digits in the sequence. Top activations are 3 or 1 being fed back at recall_idx 2, often after a repeated 3. The predicate (copy phase, L>=7, recall_idx>=2, input in that token set) gets dev F1 about 0.54 with mass recall 0.73. Precision is limited because the token and position effects are graded, not sharp.
